bull_thesis: Pluxee is a meal-voucher and employee-benefits operator that turns revenue into cash at an unusual rate: recurring free cash flow rose from about EUR 290M in FY2023 to EUR 417M in FY2025, cash conversion ran at 89% in FY2024-25 and 86% in H1 FY2026 (2026-04-16), and recurring EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation, excluding one-offs) margin reached 37% in H1 FY2026. At EUR 14.31 the company is valued at about EUR 1.97B, under five times FY2025 recurring free cash flow and about 10.6 times FY2025 earnings per share of EUR 1.35. The Brazil reform of the worker-meal programme (the PAT) is real but is already in the price: the stock trades well below its EUR 17.93 high, and the first reform quarter (Q3 FY2026, published 2026-07-03) came in better than feared - revenue EUR 312M against a consensus near EUR 299M per secondary reports, with full-year guidance confirmed. Outside Brazil the engine keeps running: record new-client wins (EUR 0.9B of annualised business volume in H1 FY2026), face-value increases in Europe, inflation-linked face values in Latin America, and a float (client money held before redemption) that earns more when rates stay high. Management has started returning cash (a EUR 0.38 dividend and a EUR 100M buyback announced 2025-10-30) and openly said the share price undervalues the company. If FY2027 earnings fall no more than 10-15% from the Brazil reset and the market pays even Edenred's de-rated ten-times forward earnings plus credit for excess cash, the shares are worth high-teens to low-twenties. Conditions: the FY2027 outlook on 2026-10-29 shows a bounded Brazil hit; no second large market caps fees; cash conversion stays near 80%.
bear_thesis: The cheapness is the market correctly pricing a smaller, politically exposed earnings base. Organic revenue went from +10.6% in FY2025 to -3.3% in Q3 FY2026, the first decline since the 2024 spin-off, and management has warned that Q4 FY2026 will show an intensified Brazil impact. The company's own earlier scenarios had Brazil revenue down by up to 40% in H2 FY2026 and up to 50% by 2027; Brazil is among the highest-margin markets, so the EBITDA hit is larger than the revenue hit, and the cut in settlement time from 30 to 15 days shrinks the float, which reverses part of the working-capital tailwind that flattered free cash flow. Regulation has now capped merchant fees in two major markets (Italy, then Brazil) - pricing power in this industry is granted and withdrawn by governments. Client headcount is shrinking in automotive, IT and staffing (CEO, 2026-04-16), net retention held at 100% only because face values rose, gross margin is contracting, and H1 FY2026 EPS of EUR 0.73 missed the EUR 0.78 estimate. The headline EUR 2.02B net cash is mostly float that belongs to the redemption cycle, not shareholders; only the excess-cash slice, which fell about EUR 140M in H1, is distributable. Sell-side is lukewarm: Oddo BHF cut its target to EUR 14 with a neutral rating on 2026-07-06. If FY2027 earnings per share drops to about EUR 1.05 and the sector multiple stays at nine times, the shares are worth about EUR 10-11. What would confirm it: a FY2027 outlook with a revenue decline and margin contraction, or another country moving to cap fees.
consensus_delta: The deep-value question is whether the market is pricing terminal decline into a business with stable earnings power. Partly yes: at under five times FY2025 recurring free cash flow (EUR 417M) the price implies a permanent fall in cash generation far beyond what the guidance says - FY2026 was confirmed on 2026-07-03 at stable organic revenue and slightly higher margins, and Q3 beat consensus. Where the street is right: Oddo BHF's neutral EUR 14 target (2026-07-06) and its expectation of a significantly heavier Brazil impact from Q4 FY2026 reflect a genuine reset that the company's own scenarios put at up to half of Brazil revenue by 2027. Where we disagree with the market: the headline net cash is not the cushion bulls cite (most is float), so the stock is not as cheap as the screener's 57% margin of safety suggests; but nor is it a melting ice cube - new-client wins are at a record and European face values are rising. Our fair value of about EUR 17.5 is roughly 22% above today's price, a real but not exceptional discount.
forcing_function: The FY2026 full-year results and FY2027 outlook on 2026-10-29. This is the first time management will quantify the Brazil reform's full-year effect. A bounded outlook (Brazil hit roughly priced in, margins defended, a renewed buyback from excess cash) would force a re-rating toward high-teens; a harsh one would confirm the bear case. A new shareholder-return programme or a disciplined acquisition announced with the results are secondary forcing events.
valley_of_death: No balance-sheet risk: the company holds net cash and no maturity wall is in our inputs. The risky window is the next three to nine months of earnings: Q4 FY2026 and H1 FY2027 carry the full Brazil fee cap and the shorter settlement period, which also drains float and therefore free cash flow through working capital. A FY2027 outlook showing a revenue decline with margin contraction would likely push the shares toward the low end of their range (EUR 9.90 was the 52-week low). European client headcount cuts in automotive, IT and staffing could add pressure. Litigation in Brazil is ongoing and could swing either way.
positioning_washout: Little forced-selling pressure is visible. The Sodexo spin-off overhang (holders dumping a spun-off share they did not choose) is largely behind it after two years of listing. Smart-money score is a middling 33 of 100 and institutional flow is neutral at 50; there is no dividend cut in prospect that would drive out yield holders - the dividend was raised 9% for FY2025. Today's 4% fall on modest volume ahead of results looks like pre-results de-risking rather than mechanical selling.
moderator_conclusion: Wait for the event: we buy once the FY2027 outlook on 2026-10-29 confirms the Brazil hit is bounded. The thesis holds - Pluxee is a well-run, cash-rich voucher franchise whose management has met or beaten every target since its 2024 listing, and at EUR 14.31 it trades at under five times last year's free cash flow. But the one number that decides the value, how much of Brazil's earnings the new fee cap permanently removes, will be published in three days, and our base fair value of about EUR 17.5 is only modestly above the 20% discount we require in the current reflation backdrop. Buying three days before the company quantifies its main risk would be paying for an answer we can have for free. The case also has limits: the headline EUR 2.02B of net cash is mostly client float rather than shareholder money, regulators have now capped fees in two big markets, and the gap to Edenred is shared sector movement rather than an edge specific to Pluxee - which is why conviction is moderate. If the outlook implies FY2027 recurring EBITDA down no more than about 15%, the discount is real and we would buy; if it shows a deeper cut with margins falling, we would pass.
sop_breakdown: Base case, whole-company: FY2027 EPS about EUR 1.30 (a mid-teens percentage cut from the FY2026 run-rate as Brazil resets, partly offset by Europe and cost discipline; about 137M shares) x 11 times forward earnings (a small premium to Edenred's 10.3 times because Pluxee converts more of its earnings to cash and carries no net debt) = EUR 14.3, plus about EUR 3.2 per share of estimated excess cash (shareholder cash beyond the float; estimate, not a disclosed figure in our inputs) = about EUR 17.5. Cross-check on cash flow: normalised recurring free cash flow of about EUR 300M after the Brazil reset and without float growth (EUR 2.2 per share) at 8 times = EUR 17.5. Kepler's last cited target of EUR 18 sits beside this; Oddo BHF's EUR 14 (2026-07-06) sits near the current price.
risk_reward: From EUR 14.31: about EUR 3.8 down to the adverse case of EUR 10.5 versus about EUR 3.2 up to the base fair value of EUR 17.5 and about EUR 8.7 up to the favourable case of EUR 23. The pipeline computes the ratios from these levels.
peer_comps_note: The anchor peer is Edenred (EDEN.PA), Pluxee's partner in a near-duopoly, now at about 10.3 times forward earnings and 4.1 times forward EBITDA (Oddo BHF and sell-side 2026 estimates, as of 2026-06) after the same Brazil and Italy reforms de-rated both - not the 20-25 times it traded at before the shock. Pluxee at about 10.6 times trailing earnings and under 5 times free cash flow is only modestly cheaper, and that gap is largely explained by Pluxee's heavier Brazil exposure. Because both names move on the same unresolved regulatory driver, any convergence between them is shared sector movement, not an edge specific to Pluxee; we give no credit for the gap as single-name alpha. We place Pluxee in line with peers.
interrogator_dossier:
# Pluxee (PLX.PA) - deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-10-26. Quote used: EUR 14.31 on Euronext Paris (FMP live quote, down about 4% on the day; 52-week range EUR 9.90-17.93). Sources: the FY2025 results call (2025-10-30), the H1 FY2026 results call (2026-04-16), the Q3 FY2026 revenue release (2026-07-03, via press coverage), and the screener's financial block. The Q1 FY2026 call is not in the transcript set. Pluxee's fiscal year ends 31 August; FY2026 full-year results are due 2026-10-29.*

**Takeaway:** Pluxee is a highly cash-generative meal-voucher and employee-benefits franchise whose management has delivered or beaten every target since its 2024 spin-off from Sodexo. The investment question is no longer execution; it is how much of the earnings base Brazil's reform of its worker-meal programme (the PAT, Programa de Alimentacao do Trabalhador) permanently removes. That number lands with the FY2027 outlook on 2026-10-29.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **FY2025 call (2025-10-30): offense.** The story was a "step change in the group's financial profile": organic revenue +10.6%, recurring EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation, excluding one-offs) margin +230 basis points, cash conversion 89%, free cash flow up from about EUR 290M (FY2023) to EUR 417M. Capital return was upgraded: a EUR 0.38 dividend (+9%) plus a first EUR 100M buyback. Italy's merchant-fee cap was presented as "almost entirely absorbed".
- **H1 FY2026 call (2026-04-16): offense on margins, defense on the top line.** Revenue EUR 655M, +5.6% organic (half the prior year's pace); recurring EBITDA EUR 242M, margin 37%. The vocabulary shifts to "resilient", "cost discipline", "AI as a key optimization enabler", and an explicit "update on the regulatory situation in Brazil". Public Benefits (state programmes in Romania and Austria) and the UK/US businesses are described as temporary drags.
- **Q3 FY2026 (2026-07-03): the reform starts to bite.** Revenue EUR 312M, -3.3% organic (Employee Benefits operating revenue -2.6%), blamed on the PAT reform's 3.6% cap on merchant fees. Guidance was confirmed at "stable" organic revenue for the year, a slight EBITDA margin expansion and around 80% cash conversion, with Q4 flagged as "intensified" Brazil impact.

The arc: from double-digit growth to a flat year, with margins and cash still defended. Growth drivers introduced: face-value increases (the legal maximum per voucher), cross-selling, SME acquisition, M&A (Beneficio Facil, Skipr, Cobee). Quietly de-emphasised: low-double-digit organic growth as a medium-term identity.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Low double-digit" organic growth FY2025 | +10.6% organic; reported revenue 1.29B (+6.4% reported, after over 7 points of currency drag) | Matches |
| EBITDA grows at twice the pace of revenue | H1 FY26 recurring EBITDA +12.9% vs revenue +5.6% | Matches through H1; H2 explicitly guided lower because of Brazil |
| Free cash flow is a structural engine | FY25 recurring FCF EUR 417M on 1.29B revenue; scan FCF margin 24%, P/FCF 7x | Matches, but partly flattered by float growth (see below) |
| Cash conversion above 75-80% | 89% FY24/FY25, 86% H1 FY26 | Over-delivered |
| Net cash 2.02B is a balance-sheet asset | The CFO himself splits it: most is float-related (client prepayments awaiting redemption); "excess cash" fell about EUR 140M in H1 to fund dividend and buyback | Richer than reality - only the excess-cash slice is shareholder money |

**Data cautions.** (1) The screener's "TTM diluted EPS 2.53" is not reconcilable with reported numbers: H1 FY26 EPS 0.73 plus H2 FY25 (FY25 1.35 minus H1 FY25 0.66) gives about 1.42. Treat 2.53 as a data artefact. (2) Altman-Z of 0.6 reflects voucher float liabilities, not distress. (3) ROE of 68% is distorted by the spin-off's low book equity (book value per share down 14% a year over five years). ROIC (return on invested capital) of 10.6% is the honest read. (4) Gross margin is flagged "contracting" - consistent with merchant-fee caps in Italy and now Brazil.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY - Stable, turning defensive

- FY2025: "another very strong year... delivered above expectations across all key metrics"; buyback framed as "a sign of our confidence" and a comment on "where the stock price is currently trading".
- H1 FY2026: "solid H1... well on track", but "a more uncertain macro and geopolitical environment"; on clients cutting staff because of AI, the CEO said "not many of them have very clear answers" and named automotive, IT and staffing as under pressure.
- Q3 FY2026: confirmation of guidance with a warning of a heavier Q4.
Guidance specificity has held up (numeric margin and conversion targets), which is a positive; confidence on the top line has clearly fallen.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY - High

FY2024-25 targets were met or beaten (growth on target, margin expansion of 230 bp vs 150 bp promised, cash conversion 89% vs >75%). New-client wins beat the EUR 1.3B annual target (EUR 1.5B). The FY2026 guidance was cut once (after the Brazil decree, to two scenarios) and then held through Q3. The earnings-beat rate in the scan is only 2 of 5 quarters (40%), and H1 FY26 EPS of 0.73 missed a 0.78 estimate - so the beats are on margins and cash, not on per-share earnings. Mild sandbagging on EBITDA guidance (H1 beat, full year reiterated) was questioned by UBS on 2026-04-16; the CFO attributed it to Brazil, not conservatism.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Brazil**: the dominant question. Management will not restructure Brazil yet, wanting to "benefit from all potential scenarios" (2026-04-16) - i.e. they are hedging on litigation and on how the market structure settles.
- **Use of cash** (Deutsche Bank): answer was M&A "in a very rigorous and disciplined manner" - no new return programme promised.
- **End-user portfolio** (UBS, Bernstein): headcount at clients is shrinking in some sectors; net retention held at 100% only because face values rose.
- **Cross-selling** (Bernstein, 2025-10-30): management declined to size non-meal-voucher revenue.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: Q3 FY26 organic revenue -3.3% - the first decline since listing (2026-07-03).
- Red: earlier company scenarios of Brazil revenue down up to 40% in H2 FY26 and up to 50% by 2027; the 3.6% merchant-fee cap and the cut in settlement time from 30 to 15 days shrink both take rate and float.
- Red: regulation is now hitting two of the largest markets (Italy fee cap, Brazil PAT) - the pricing power is political, not contractual.
- Red: client headcount pressure (automotive, IT, staffing), H1 FY26.
- Green: cash conversion 86-89% for two and a half years; free cash flow EUR 417M in FY25.
- Green: shareholder returns started (dividend + EUR 100M buyback), with an explicit nod to the low share price.
- Green: record new-client wins (EUR 0.9B annualised business volume in H1 FY26) and over 30% from SMEs.
- Green: Q3 revenue beat consensus (about EUR 312M vs 299M per secondary reports) and the stock rose about 6% - the Brazil hit arrived smaller than feared.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The CFO's insistence on separating "excess cash" from float-related cash (2026-04-16) is an honest disclosure that signals the headline net cash should not be capitalised.
- "Not engaging right now in a pool of restructuring" in Brazil: a cost response is being held back until the regulatory outcome is clear - upside if the reform softens, a cost-cut lever later if not.
- AI language moved from product ("chatbots", FY25) to cost ("optimization enabler", H1 FY26) - margins are increasingly self-help.
- Same CEO and CFO across both calls; no management changes.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: stable.** Execution and cash discipline are strong; the top line is being reset by regulation, not by a loss of competitiveness.

**The single thing to weigh:** the size of the permanent Brazil cut. At EUR 14.31 the market value is about EUR 1.97B, roughly 4.7 times FY25 recurring free cash flow - cheap if FY2027 earnings are down 10-15%, fair if they are down 30%+. The FY2027 outlook on 2026-10-29 answers this.

**Moat:** a narrow but real moat - a two-sided network (employers on one side, an affiliated merchant network on the other) plus scale and regulatory licensing, in a market shared with Edenred. The returns evidence is mixed: EBITDA margin expanded strongly (37% in H1 FY26), but gross margin is contracting and regulators in Italy and Brazil have now capped the merchant side of the take rate. That is a moat whose pricing is being eroded by regulation, not one being competed away. **Secular threat: material, not terminal** - the force is regulatory fee-capping plus a push toward open-loop, interoperable payment rails (payments disintermediation of the closed voucher network). The cheapness is partly a fear-print (cash generation intact) and partly a genuinely smaller Brazilian earnings base; it is not a structurally shrinking whole.

interrogator_dossier:
# Pluxee (PLX.PA) - deep dive on management and the setup
*As of 2026-11-16. Live price EUR 12.24 on Euronext Paris (FMP quote). Transcripts read: full-year fiscal 2025 (2025-10-30), first half fiscal 2026 (2026-04-16), full-year fiscal 2026 (2026-10-29). Pluxee's fiscal year ends 31 August.*

**Bottom line:** Pluxee is a well-run meal-voucher and employee-benefits network that keeps beating the targets it sets, but its two largest markets are being rewritten by regulators at the same time. Brazil's food-programme reform (decree published 2025-11-12) caps merchant fees and shortens settlement, and France's voucher law is still moving through Parliament. Management's credibility on execution is high; its ability to forecast regulation is not something any management has. The stock at EUR 12.24 is cheap on trailing earnings, but fiscal 2027 is a guided step down and the size of the rebase is not yet proven.

One forensic correction matters before anything else: the screener's "net cash EUR 2.26B" is not money the shareholders own. Most of it is float (customers pre-fund vouchers; Pluxee holds the cash until merchants are paid). The fiscal 2026 release shows EUR 3,906M of "value in circulation and related payables" against it, and only EUR 548M of cash not related to float, against EUR 1,281M of gross bond and bank debt. Stripped of float, the corporate balance sheet carries roughly EUR 0.73B of net debt. The float earns a yield (EUR 166M of float revenue in fiscal 2026, at 6.2%) that already sits inside EBITDA and earnings, so adding the float cash on top of an earnings multiple would count it twice.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
- **Fiscal 2025 call (2025-10-30): growth and capital return.** "Another very strong year": organic revenue +10.6%, recurring EBITDA margin +230bp, cash conversion 89%, free cash flow up from about EUR 290M (fiscal 2023) to EUR 417M. First buyback (EUR 100M). Brazil was barely mentioned beyond a Santander partnership win.
- **First half fiscal 2026 (2026-04-16): resilience language arrives.** Revenue growth slowed to +5.6% organic; "increasingly challenging environment"; Public Benefits in Europe and the UK/US now a drag. Brazil appears as a regulatory section; the CFO says the reform "will weigh a lot" on second-half margin.
- **Full-year fiscal 2026 (2026-10-29): "transition year".** Total revenue +0.7% organic to EUR 1,302M; recurring EBITDA EUR 488M (37.5% margin); cash conversion fell to 70%. Fiscal 2027 guided to at least EUR 440M EBITDA (about 10% lower) and at least 50% cash conversion, with no revenue guidance. The emphasis moves to cost efficiency, AI, and a higher payout (40%, dividend EUR 0.65).

The story contracted from "low double-digit growth compounder" to "cash-generative franchise working through a regulatory rebase" in twelve months.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
| Claim | Evidence | Read |
|---|---|---|
| "Delivered ahead of all financial objectives" (FY26) | Revenue +0.7% vs a "stable" target; EBITDA margin +101bp vs "slight" expansion; 3-year conversion 82% vs "around 80%" | True, but the targets were cut in November 2025 after the Brazil decree. Beat a lowered bar. |
| EBITDA grows twice as fast as revenue (H1 FY26) | FY26 EBITDA +3.8% organic vs revenue +0.7% | Holds, driven by flat opex (EUR 840M vs 816M reported, roughly flat at constant scope) |
| Strong cash generation | Recurring FCF EUR 341M (FY26) vs 417M (FY25) | Fell 18%; Brazil settlement shortening drains float. FY27 guided to at least 50% conversion, about EUR 220M |
| Earnings growth | Adjusted EPS EUR 1.58 (+4.4%) but reported EPS EUR 1.21 (-10.8%); operating profit -12% | Gap of EUR 53M between adjusted and reported net profit (acquired-intangible amortization, restructuring, UK/US exit). Watch that "non-recurring" does not recur. |
| Net retention near 100% | 99.4% (FY26) vs 100% (FY25) | Face-value increases (EUR 1.1B of volume) and cross-selling offset falling headcount at clients. Underlying users are shrinking in Continental Europe. |
| Brazil is a contained "rebase" | Latin America operating revenue +1.1% organic, +8.2% ex the fee cap | The cap is visible; the fiscal 2027 "extended rebase" (equalizing merchant terms across all programmes) is a management choice that deepens the hit before it eases |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY - Declining
- FY25: "outstanding cash generation", "well ahead of our initial plan".
- H1 FY26: "more uncertain macro and geopolitical environment"; clients under pressure in automotive, IT and staffing ("reading some of their budgets").
- FY26: "transition year", "subdued macroeconomic environment" in France, "the low hanging fruit have been raised" on costs. Guidance became less specific (no revenue line). Defensive turn is clear.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY - Medium-High
Pluxee has met or beaten every numeric target it has set since the 2024 spin-off from Sodexo, including the H1 FY26 beat and the FY26 EBITDA of EUR 488M vs a EUR 474M company-compiled consensus. But it lowered fiscal 2026 targets after the Brazil decree (November 2025), and the fiscal 2027 guide fell short of sell-side expectations (J.P. Morgan comment; shares fell about 13% on 2026-10-29). The pattern is conservative-and-beat on what it controls, with no edge on regulation. The screener's 2-of-5 quarterly beat rate reflects the regulatory resets, not missed internal targets.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
- **Size and duration of the Brazil hit.** Asked on every call; management gives direction ("intensify in H1, dissipate from H2") but no revenue number.
- **Cash use.** Deutsche Bank (H1 FY26) asked about the cash pile; the CFO had to explain that most of the rise was float, while excess cash fell EUR 140M in the half. Confirms the float caveat above.
- **France.** Barclays (FY26) on the draft voucher law: it passed the lower house on 2026-10-12 and goes to the Senate in November; it gives the government the power to cap merchant fees after an antitrust opinion. Management calls it "a safeguard"; that is the bull reading.
- **Is EBITDA guidance conservative?** UBS (H1 FY26); the CFO said no.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
- Red: Regulators in Brazil (2025-11-12 decree), Italy (merchant-fee cap, FY25) and potentially France (fee-cap power in the draft law, 2026-10-12) are all compressing the merchant side of the take rate at once.
- Red: Cash conversion guided down to at least 50% for FY27 - float is leaving as settlement shortens.
- Red: Reported EPS falling while adjusted EPS rises.
- Red: End-user volumes shrinking in Continental Europe (FY26 call).
- Green: Opex held flat in nominal terms despite about 5% weighted inflation and 4.5% more volume (FY26 call).
- Green: New-client wins at a record EUR 1.5B annualized volume in both FY25 and FY26; SMEs over 32%.
- Green: Investment-grade rating affirmed by S&P; payout raised to 40%; EUR 100M buyback completed May 2026 (8.35M shares, 70% cancelled).

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
- The CFO now separates "net excess cash" from float-related cash unprompted - a quiet admission that the headline cash number overstates what is free.
- "Extended rebase scenario" is new vocabulary: management chose to equalize Brazilian merchant terms across all programmes, accepting a bigger near-term hit to defend share. That is a competitive move against Edenred and new open-arrangement entrants, not just compliance.
- AI is pitched both as an efficiency lever and as a client risk (clients "wondering what would be the future of their organization").

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT
**Trajectory: DETERIORATING** in reported numbers through fiscal 2027, with a credible recovery case thereafter. The single most important thing for the director: the stock is cheap on trailing earnings (about 7.7x adjusted EPS of EUR 1.58) but fiscal 2027 earnings fall, and France's law (Senate, end-2026) is an unresolved second regulatory front. Do not credit the EUR 2.26B "net cash" - it is customer float; ex-float the company carries modest net debt.

**Moat:** network plus regulatory-licence. A two-sided network (clients, about 28 countries of merchants, users) in a near-duopoly with Edenred, protected by the tax-advantaged status of meal benefits. Returns are high on tiny equity (ROE about 73%, ROIC about 10.5%) and the EBITDA margin is still rising, but the merchant-fee leg of the take rate is being capped by regulators market by market, and the scan shows gross margin contracting. The moat is real but narrowing on price; I rate it NARROW with an eroding trend.

**Secular threat:** material, not terminal. Open-arrangement and interoperability rules (Brazil) and fee caps push the product toward a regulated, lower-margin payment rail - a form of payments disintermediation. The tax incentive that creates the market is not being removed, and France is moving to make the card permanent for all food purchases. The cheapness is part fear-print, part genuine rebase.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory weakening · a narrow but real moat · moat trend eroding · structural threat material.

The claim is not disproven but not yet shown, and the first half of fiscal 2027 is where the hit peaks.
